article.name: CAMEL

contact.note: The official pinned README publishes camel-ai@eigent.ai under Community & Contact.

article.summary: CAMEL is a multi-agent framework with a modular memory package. Its memory interfaces represent message records, adapt chat-history and vector stores, and assemble records into agent context. The defaults are in-memory stores; long-term memory combines conversation history with vector recall. This is a source review, not a measured evaluation.

who_what.text: CAMEL is a multi-agent framework; its memory package offers chat-history and vector-memory components that integrate with ChatAgent.

architecture.text: AgentMemory extends the memory-block contract with retrieval and context-creation operations. ChatAgent defaults to ChatHistoryMemory; the memory wrappers allow callers to inject alternate storage backends.
MemoryRecord stores a message, backend role, UUID, timestamp, string metadata, and agent_id. Vector payloads preserve the serialized record, so the indexed unit remains a message.
ChatHistoryMemory defaults to in-memory key-value storage. VectorDBBlock defaults to OpenAIEmbedding and in-memory Qdrant; LongtermAgentMemory composes chat and vector blocks.

behavior.text: Write — chat history serializes and appends records. Vector memory embeds nonempty message text and stores vectors with record payloads; LongtermAgentMemory writes to both stores and tracks the latest user message as its current topic.

Update/delete — chat history supports pop, selected-index removal, and clear, preserving an initial system/developer message during indexed or pop removal. Vector memory does not support individual pop/index removal and exposes clear; combined long-term pop/index operations modify chat history while vector records remain.

Retrieval — chat history returns all records or a bounded recent window. Vector retrieval embeds the current topic and requests top-k similar records; the memory block constructs a query without an agent or tenant filter.

Scope isolation — wrappers attach agent_id to records, but the inspected vector query does not filter by it. The core memory path alone therefore does not establish tenant isolation; isolation depends on storage configuration or backend behavior.

Provenance/evidence — records retain role, time, UUID, and optional metadata. The inspected record and vector interfaces do not add claim-level citations, trust/confidence states, or edit audit history.

metrics.evidence: The vector path selects top-k by similarity, but no judged answer-quality or abstention workload was run.
Chat history exposes record removal while vector memory lacks individual removal; no correction workload was run.
No post-delete retrieval or deletion leakage probe was run.
The inspected vector query has no scope filter; no cross-agent isolation workload was run.
Records contain role and metadata fields, but no claim-support evaluation was run.
Top-k bounds vector results, but no latency, tokens, cost, storage, or memory-specific telemetry measurements were collected.

limits.text: Default stores are in-memory. Durable persistence requires a configured backend; vector records cannot be individually removed through the reviewed memory API.
The reviewed core vector-memory query does not filter on agent_id. Production isolation, retention, and security depend on selected backend and deployment configuration and were not tested here.
This is source inspection at the verified master head. It does not establish runtime behavior, retrieval quality, isolation, performance, or behavior of every optional backend integration.

benchmark.text: Benchmark status is not_run. Project metrics, fixtures, and execution status describe evaluation protocol and project state, not CAMEL results. No CAMEL system, benchmark, or tests were run.
